status_summary: The United States continues to decline to support the proposal by WTO members to launch Appellate Body appointments: at the Dispute Settlement Body meetings of 2026-06-23, 2026-07-24 and 2026-09-25 it said its fundamental concerns with dispute settlement had not been addressed and that the proposal (WT/DSB/W/609/Rev.26) would restore the conditions that produced them. USTR's WTO reform paper of 2026-03-23 (WT/GC/W/998) does not address the Appellate Body, proposes that essential security measures be self-judging and not adjudicated, and suggests interim and, if needed, non-WTO plurilateral agreements among subsets of members, not an alliance limited to liberal democracies. No successor organization or Global Free Trade Alliance proposal was found.

title: Restore WTO dispute settlement or build a successor alliance of liberal democracies
uncertainties: The US statements of 2026-06-23, 2026-07-24 and 2026-09-25 were read on USTR's site; the USTR listing showed no October 2026 Dispute Settlement Body statement as of 2026-10-26. The figures of 130 supporting members and a 98th block, from a Third World Network (SUNS) report (a lead host, not cited), were not verified on WTO.org, which could not be fetched, and are omitted from the summary. The Rev.26 designation appears in the June and July statements as well as the September one as read; the revision numbering was not checked against WTO documents. Two searches for a Global Free Trade Alliance proposal found none, but absence rests on limited searching. The essay itself notes that both prior administrations kept the blockade, so this is a continuation rather than a reversal; it is staged diverged because the operative US position at each meeting is opposite to restoring the Appellate Body. The reform paper's non-WTO plurilaterals are not restricted to liberal democracies and are not a successor body, so they do not meet the fallback recommendation. USTR's statements at the General Council meeting of 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-06 (listed on USTR's site) were read on 2026-10-26 and do not address dispute settlement, the Appellate Body or a successor body.
